title: What If Light Moved at Walking Speed? Colours Would Flip as You Walk

scenes.text: What if light moved at walking speed? Every step would change the colour of the world.
scenes.keywords: person walking city street motion blur

scenes.text: Light does 300,000 kilometres a second. The fastest humans have ever gone is 0.0037 percent of that, so relativity stays hidden.
Slow light down and walking becomes near light speed. Whatever you walk toward shifts blue. Whatever is behind you turns red.
Things ahead look brighter too, because you're walking into their photons. Physicists call it the searchlight effect.
Time runs slower for you than for someone standing still. A passing bicycle wouldn't look shorter, as the textbook says. It would look stretched and warped.
MIT built this world as a video game in 2012. Pick up 100 orbs and light slows, step by step, until a stroll becomes a trip through Einstein's maths.

description:
What if the speed of light dropped to walking speed? Light covers about 300,000 kilometres a second, and the fastest any human has travelled is about 0.0037 percent of that, so the effects of special relativity stay invisible. With light slowed to a stroll, every walk would be a near-light-speed trip: objects ahead shift blue and brighten through the Doppler and searchlight effects, objects behind shift red, time runs slower for the walker, and moving objects appear warped and even stretched because light from their near side arrives first.
MIT Game Lab physicists Gerd Kortemeyer and Philip Tan built this world in the 2012 game A Slower Speed of Light, where collecting 100 orbs lowers the speed of light step by step. In reality the speed of light in a vacuum never changes.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: George Gamow wrote a picture book about this in 1939, and Einstein reportedly loved it. What law of physics would you change for a day? Drop your own what-if below.
